q_45395.question_text: Will a U.S. federal agency announce new or expanded model evaluation agreements with both OpenAI and Anthropic before September 3, 2026?
q_45395.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
From August 15, 2026 to September 3, 2026 = **19 days**. This is an extremely tight timeframe for federal agency announcements.

## (b) Status quo outcome if nothing changes
CAISI already has existing agreements with both OpenAI and Anthropic (established August 29, 2024). These were updated on May 4, 2026. Without new announcements, the question resolves NO. The status quo is that pre-existing arrangements remain in place.

## (c) Scenario for NO outcome
No federal agency announces new or materially expanded agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic between August 10 and September 3, 2026. This is the baseline—federal agencies rarely announce major new agreements on short notice, and 19 days is a very compressed timeframe for bureaucratic processes.

## (d) Scenario for YES outcome
A U.S. federal agency (likely CAISI/NIST) announces either:
- A new agreement with OpenAI covering a previously uncovered model family, access arrangement, testing scope, or evaluation domain, AND
- A new or expanded agreement with Anthropic covering similar new territory

OR announcements of expansions to existing arrangements that explicitly identify previously not-covered dimensions. The two announcements need not be simultaneous but both must occur by September 3.

## (e) Base rate
The research provided shows:
- Initial CAISI agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic: August 29, 2024
- Expansion announcements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI: May 5, 2026
- Time between major tranches of announcement: ~9 months

The research also notes that agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic were "updated on May 4, 2026," but explicitly states this May 5, 2026 announcement "did not explicitly mention new or expanded agreements *with OpenAI and Anthropic*." This suggests that while updates occurred, they were not prominently announced as major new developments.

**No reliable base rate for announcements within 19-day windows** can be established from the provided information, but the pattern suggests CAISI batches announcements periodically (May 2026 was a major announcement window; prior was August 2024).

## (f) How the live data/research moves from base rate

**Factors pushing toward YES (19% weight):**
- A White House meeting on August 3, 2026 discussed a voluntary framework for testing advanced AI models, explicitly including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google
- This recent meeting suggests policy momentum and near-term action possibility
- Existing arrangements with both companies were updated May 4, 2026, showing ongoing engagement
- The narrow window (19 days) suggests the question setter may have specific knowledge of imminent announcements

**Factors pushing strongly toward NO (81% weight):**
- Federal agency announcements typically follow deliberate planning cycles; 19 days is very compressed
- CAISI's last major announcement batch was May 5, 2026 (3+ months ago); announcing again so soon would be unusual
- The resolution criteria require "new or materially expanded" agreements—not just updates or discussions
- The research explicitly notes that the May 4, 2026 updates to OpenAI/Anthropic agreements were not highlighted as major new announcements
- A White House meeting is not equivalent to a federal agency announcement of new evaluation agreements
- Bureaucratic processes for formal announcement require time (legal review, clearance, joint messaging coordination)
- The question specifically requires announcements "after August 10 and before September 3"—if these were already planned, they likely would have been announced during the May window

## (g) Community prediction

No current community prediction is provided in this message. I must rely on the analysis above.

---

## Reasoning Summary

The question requires announcements of new or materially expanded evaluation agreements with **both** OpenAI and Anthropic within 19 days. While there is suggestive evidence of ongoing policy momentum (the August 3 White House meeting), the base operational reality is:

1. CAISI's major announcements follow deliberate scheduling (previous major announcement: May 5, 2026)
2. Existing agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic were already updated May 4, 2026, but not prominently re-announced
3. 19 days is an extremely short window for federal agency announcements requiring coordination, legal review, and official messaging
4. The resolution criteria are specific about requiring explicit announcements of "new or materially expanded" arrangements—meetings and discussions don't count

The White House meeting provides some signal of policy momentum, but it alone doesn't justify high confidence in formal agency announcements within such a tight timeframe. Federal bureaucracies move slower than 19-day windows typically allow for formal agreement announcements.

**Probability: 18%**
q_45395.research_text:
A U.S. federal agency, the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) within the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), already has evaluation agreements with both OpenAI and Anthropic. These initial agreements were announced on August 29, 2024, by the U.S. AI Safety Institute (which was re-established as CAISI in June 2025) to enable formal collaboration on AI safety research, testing, and evaluation [nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/08/us-ai-safety-institute-signs-agreements-regarding-ai-safety-research), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/08/29/openai-and-anthropic-agree-to-let-us-ai-safety-institute-test-models).

On May 5, 2026, CAISI announced new, expanded agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI, building on previously existing partnerships to conduct pre-deployment evaluations and targeted research for assessing frontier AI capabilities and advancing AI security [nist.gov](https://web.archive.org/web/20260505134747/https:/www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/05/caisi-signs-agreements-regarding-frontier-ai-national-security-testing), [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/924017/google-microsoft-xai-government-review). These agreements support testing in classified environments and allow developers to provide models with reduced safeguards for thorough evaluation. CAISI has completed over 40 such evaluations to date [nist.gov](https://web.archive.org/web/20260505134747/https:/www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/05/caisi-signs-agreements-regarding-frontier-ai-national-security-testing). While the May 5, 2026, announcement did not explicitly mention new or expanded agreements *with OpenAI and Anthropic*, the existing agreements with these companies were updated on May 4, 2026 [nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/08/us-ai-safety-institute-signs-agreements-regarding-ai-safety-research). A White House meeting on August 3, 2026, to discuss a new voluntary framework for testing advanced AI models, is expected to include representatives from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/03/white-house-ai-companies-voluntary-framework-meeting.html). This framework is for voluntary participation, not mandatory licensing.

NVIDIA has already provided forward guidance for its second quarter of fiscal year 2027. On May 20, 2026, the company announced its outlook, stating that revenue is expected to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This guidance does not include any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027).

For the same period, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 74.9% and 75.0% respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are projected to be approximately $8.5 billion and $8.3 billion, respectively [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). Analysts, according to LSEG, had an average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion for Q2 FY2027, making Nvidia's guidance well above this average [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).
